findings.sentence: Stipend (living allowance) at the rate of £1,712 per month, or £2,000 per month for those at universities in the London metropolitan area (rates quoted at current levels) – paid and funded by the university.
findings.note: Distinct amounts on one page: £1,712 (commonwealth-shared-7); £154 (commonwealth-shared-7); £2,000 (commonwealth-shared-7); £622 (commonwealth-shared-7).
findings.resolution: Different fields. £1,712 per month (£2,000 in the London metropolitan area) is the stipend (living allowance); £622 / £154 per month are child allowances for a widowed, divorced or single-parent Scholar (first child / second and third child under 16). Quote the stipend with the London uplift, and the child allowances only as child allowances.
findings.resolution_evidence: Stipend (living allowance) at the rate of £1,712 per month, or £2,000 per month for those at universities in the London metropolitan area. Child allowance of £622 per month for the first child, and £154 per month for the second and third child under the age of 16.

findings.sentence: France Excellence Eiffel scholarship holders receive a monthly allowance of €1,200 (from January 2026), to which is added several services: International transportation, national transportation, insurance, housing searches, cultural activities, etc.
findings.note: Distinct amounts on one page: €1,200 (eiffel-1); €2,000 (eiffel-1).
findings.resolution: Not a contradiction. The page gives the amounts under separate level headings: €1,200/month is the Master's level allowance, €2,000/month is the Doctorate level stipend, both from January 2026. Tuition fees are not covered at either level.
findings.resolution_evidence: Master's level. France Excellence Eiffel scholarship holders receive a monthly allowance of €1,200 (from January 2026). Doctorate level. France Excellence Eiffel scholarship holders receive a monthly stipend of €2,000 (from January 2026).

findings.sentence: Grant per project: up to €5 million.
findings.note: Distinct amounts on one page: €1,400 (erasmus-mundus-org-0); €5 (erasmus-mundus-org-0).
findings.resolution: Not a contradiction. The two amounts are different fields: €5 million is the maximum grant per EMJM project (to the consortium), €1,400 per month is the EU scholarship paid to an individual student (max. 24 months). Quote each with its field.
findings.resolution_evidence: Grant per project: up to €5 million. EU scholarship for individuals: €1,400 per month (max. 24 months).

findings.sentence: The Gates Cambridge Scholarship programme was established in October 2000 by an historic donation of US$210m from the Gates Foundation to the University of Cambridge.
findings.note: Distinct amounts on one page: US$210 (gates-cambridge-0); £12,793 (gates-cambridge-1); £18,244 (gates-cambridge-1); £23,152 (gates-cambridge-0); £4,000 (gates-cambridge-1); £750 (gates-cambridge-1).
findings.resolution: Different fields, plus a donation. £23,152 is the maintenance allowance for a single student (2026-27 rate, 12 months); £750–£4,000 is discretionary academic development funding; £12,793 / £18,244 per annum is the Dependent Children Allowance (one child / two or more); US$210m is the Trust's founding donation from 2000, not a stipend. The checker counts 'a money amount appears', not 'a stipend is stated' — the donation is why Gates was never flagged missing even before the £ fix.
findings.resolution_evidence: a maintenance allowance for a single student (£23,152 for 12 months at the 2026-27 rate). The Gates Cambridge Scholarship programme was established in October 2000 by an historic donation of US$210m from the Gates Foundation.

findings.sentence: For the 2026-27 academic year, the stipend is £21,060 paid in monthly instalments of £1,755, from which Scholars pay all living expenses, including accommodation.
findings.note: Distinct amounts on one page: £1,755 (rhodes-0); £21,060 (rhodes-0); £6,950 (rhodes-11).
findings.resolution: Not three stipends. £21,060 is the annual stipend for 2026-27; £1,755 is the same stipend paid in monthly instalments (£21,060 / 12); £6,950 is not a payment at all — it is 33% of the annual stipend, the threshold above which a secondary award must be declared to the Registrar.
findings.resolution_evidence: For the 2026-27 academic year, the stipend is £21,060 paid in monthly instalments of £1,755. If the value of such an award is more than 33% of the annual stipend, i.e. £6,950 pa, then you would need to declare the award.

findings.sentence: RTP stipend rates: Year 2027, Full-time base RTP stipend rate ($) 35,550, Full-time max RTP stipend rate ($) 55,537.
findings.resolution: One table, six rates: a base and a maximum rate for each year. Full-time base RTP stipend rate ($) 35,550 (2027), 34,315 (2026), 33,511 (2025); maximum 55,537 (2027), 53,608 (2026), 52,352 (2025). The rates are indexed each 1 January and the next year's are announced by 1 October. Golden q29 quotes the 2026 base rate, $34,315 — quote any rate with its year and base/maximum label.
findings.resolution_evidence: Full-time base RTP stipend rate ($) 35,550 (2027). Full-time base RTP stipend rate ($) 34,315 (2026). The RTP base and maximum stipend rates are indexed each year, effective from 1 January.
